summary: Retrieve one known record by its FileMaker record ID or OData key.
purpose: Use this when you already know the record you want and need a single-record example.
learningGoals: Understand the difference between a FileMaker record ID and an OData key.
Practice a minimal read-only request with one required identifier.
See the same safe browser pattern used for a direct record fetch.
explanation: This module is a simple single-record read. It keeps the generated request small and highlights that the same record identifier can mean different things depending on the transport.
commonMistakes: Using a display value instead of the real record ID or primary key.
Forgetting that OData keys belong to tables, not layouts.
Trying to embed credentials in browser code.
expectedResult: You get starter code that fetches one record through the selected transport without mutating data.

prerequisites: Know the record ID or table key you want to fetch.
Use the protected same-origin PHP bridge for browser testing.

inputs.label: Layout or table
inputs.help: Needed for OData and helpful context for Data API users.

inputs.label: Record ID or key
inputs.help: For Data API this is usually the FileMaker record ID. For OData it is the table key or ROWID.

php:data-api.template:
// Data API: get one FileMaker record
$result = $bridge->getRecord('{{php:recordId}}');

beginner: Get one record is a safe read-only request when you already know the record you want.
The browser still calls the same-origin PHP bridge so credentials stay server-side.
OData keys can differ from FileMaker record IDs, so confirm which identifier you have.
advanced: This module intentionally keeps the payload minimal so fixture assertions stay stable.
Resource is retained as metadata even when the Data API PHP call does not reference it directly.
The PHP templates match the original playground output exactly after substitution.
